The results suggest that female college students with ADHD are at higher risk for unprotected sex, but also indicate that a positive mother-child relationship may provide some level of protection against this risk.

These findings across multiple prompts suggest a strong correlation between substance use and HIV-related sexual behaviors among US high school students. It is essential to address these issues through comprehensive prevention programs that acknowledge the complex interplay between substance use, mental health, and behaviors related to safe sex practices.

Overall, it seems clear that addressing substance use as an important factor in understanding and preventing HIV-related sexual behaviors among high school students will be crucial for developing effective public health strategies.
